full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the defendant-petitioner Md Jamal Hossain is directed against the judgment and order dated 11-5-2003 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Sagata, Gaibandha, in Money Suit No. 3 of 2002. The petitioner filed this Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 2003 for transferring the Money Suit No. 3 of 2002 from the court of Assistant Judge, Sagata, Gaibandha to any other competent Court in the District of Bogra or any other District. 

 3. The plaintiff's case, in short, is that the plaintiff-opposite party is a permanent resident of Sagata Police Station, District Gaibandha; that the plaintiff-opposite party and defendant-petitioner both are jute businessmen and the defendant-petitioner rented a godown at Borathkhali union under the police station Sagata on 5-5-2002; that he started his business under the name and style of Brothers Inter-national, that the plaintiff-opposite party sold huge quantity of jute to the defendant-petitioner in cash and credit; that in this way a friendship was grown between them and thereafter the defendant received Taka 3,00,000 only from the plaintiff-opposite party as a loan and when the plaintiff-opposite party requested the defendant-petitioner to repay the same, then the defendant-petitioner issued a cheque for Taka 3,00,000 only on 26-10-2001 and that the plaintiff-opposite party presented the said cheque to the Sonali Bank, Local Office, Dhaka for drawing cash money on 4-11-2001, 2-10-2002 and 25-4-2002 respectively. But the cheque was dishonored by the said bank, and after dishonor of the cheque by bank, the plaintiff-opposite party requested the defendant-petitioner to repay the said amount. But he refused to repay the same and hence the money suit was filed against the defendant-petitioner. 

 4. After filing of the suit, the summons was served upon the defendant-petitioner and thereafter the defendant-petitioner appeared before the court and appointed an Advocate on his behalf for contesting the case. 

 5. The further case of the defendant-petitioner is that on 23-4-2003 the engaged lawyer informed the defendant-petitioner that he is unable to contest the case in his favour and accordingly, he withdrew the vokalatnama from the court in due course; that the defendant-petitioner went to the court for appointing another lawyer for contesting the case but all the lawyers of Gaibandha Bar refused to contest the case in favour of the defendant-petitioner. 

 6. It is further stated that on 11-5-2003 the case was fixed for submission of written statement. But due to non-availability of the lawyers, the written statement could not be filed and the trial Court passed an order to the effect that in the case of failure of the defendant-petitioner to engage a lawyer, the suit will be deemed to have been decreed ex parte on the next date, which is on 11-6-2003. 

 8. Mr Nazmul Haque, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the plaintiff-opposite party is a local influential man and due to the influence of the plaintiff-opposite party, the local lawyers are not agreeable to contest the case in his favour and, as such, if the case is not transferred and with-drawn to any other competent court in the district of Bogra or to any other District the defendant-petitioner will suffer serious loss and injury. 

 9. Mr Fazle Rabbi, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party, submits that the application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for transferring the case from Gaibandha Assistant Judge Court to any other competent court in the District of Bogra or to any other district is not at all legal or proper. He further submits that there are about 350 Advocates in Gaibandha Bar and their duty is to assist the litigants; that there is no ground of refusal to accept his brief by the Advocate and there is no ground of non-availability of advocate. He further submits that the defendant-petitioner did not mention name of any of the learned Advocates who refused to accept his brief and he further submits that defendant-petitioner has filed this Civil Miscellaneous Case only to delay or obstruct the proceeding and to harass the plaintiff-opposite party. 

 11. The transfer of the case from Saghata Assistant Judge's Court to any competent court of another district is the main contention of the present revision. 

 12. Now let us see the law regarding the transfer of a case which is enumerated in section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 (2) where any suit or proceeding has been transferred or withdrawn under section (1) the Court which thereafter tries such suit may, subject to any special directions in the case of any order of transfer, either retry it or proceed from the point at which it was transferred or withdrawn. 

 24A (1) Where any suit is transferred under section 22, or any suit, appeal or other proceeding is transferred or withdrawn under sub-section (1) of section 24 on the application of a party, the court ordering the transfer or withdrawal shall fix a date for appearance of the parties before itself, if the suit, appeal or other proceeding is to be tried or disposed of by itself, or before the Court to which the case is so transferred. 

 13. As a general rule, a plaintiff as arbiter litis or dominos litis has a right to choose his own forum where there is more than one court in which the suit can be filed. But the said right is controlled by the power vested in the superior courts to transfer a case pending in one inferior court to another or to withdraw the case to itself for hearing and disposal. 

 14. Before transfer is ordered, two conditions must be satisfied namely (I) the application must be made at the earliest possible opportunity and in all cases where issues are settled, at or before the settlement of issues; and (ii) notice must be given to the other side. The provision as to notice is mandatory. Such notice may be given by the party making an application or by the court. 

 16. The court can pass such order if it is satisfied that such an order is "expedient for the ends of justice." In the light of the decisions of the apex Courts of this sub-continent, we decide grounds for transfer and not transfer of the cases. The following have been held to be sufficient grounds for transfer: (I) reasonable apprehension in the mind of the litigant that he might not get justice in the court in which the suit is pending. (ii) to avoid multiplicity of proceedings or conflicting decisions, (iii) where the judge is interested in one party or biased against the other (iv) where common questions of fact and law arise between the parties in two suits (v) on the ground of balance of convenience e.g. where the property is situated or parties reside; or the account books are kept, etc. (vi) where two persons have filed suits against each other in different courts on the same cause of action (vii) to avoid delay and unnecessary expenses (viii) where important questions of law are involved or considerable section of public is interested in the litigation (ix) to prevent abuse of the process of court; 

 17. The following, on the other hand, have been held not to be sufficient grounds for transfer: (i) mere fact that the opposite party is a man of influence in the locality, (ii) mere fact that the court is situated at a long distance from the place of the residence of the applicant (iii) mere fact that the presiding officer belongs to a community rival to that of the applicant (iv) mere fact that the judge has decided a similar point in a previous case (v) mere balance of convenience to the applicant (vi) refusal. to grant adjournment (vii) prejudice of a judge against party's pleader not likely to affect the party (viii) Judge making adverse remarks regarding merits of the case; (ix) allegation of apprehension against fair trial without furnishing particulars (x) one Counsel losing temper and using unparliamentary language, the judge ordering adjournment, etc. 

 18. Now let us see as to whether the facts and circumstances of the case are fit for transfer of the instant suit in the light of above legal position. 

 20. The contention of the defendant-petitioner is that the plaintiff-opposite party is a local influential man and due to his influence, the local lawyers are not agreeable to contest the case in favour of the defendant-opposite party and, as such, if the case is not transferred to any other competent Court in the district of Bogra or to any other district, the defendant-petitioner swill suffer serious loss and injury. 

 21. The mere allegation that due to the influence of the plaintiff-opposite party, the Advocates of Gibandha Bar are not agreeable to contest the suit in favour of the defendant-petitioner is not sufficient to withdraw and transfer a case from one district to another district unless such allegation is backed by sufficient grounds. 

 24. We have already seen that the established principle of law that the burden of establishing sufficient grounds for transfer lies heavily upon the applicant. But the defendant-petitioner totally failed to show any sufficient ground for transfer of the case. Application on such wishful assumption should be discouraged. The court cannot allow a transfer petition on a mere allegation. 

 26. Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure does not enjoin any condition for transfer. But such transfer can only be made upon some established principles and by exercise of proper judicial discretion. Here, in this case, there is no cogent ground to justify such transfer. Rather, such transfer of the case will create immense trouble to both parties and also will incur huge cost of booth parties. 

 27. The consistent view of our courts is, that the power to transfer a case from one Court to another is a discretionary power of the court which should be exercised judiciously. In this revision, there is no material on record to exercise such discretion. 

 28. It further appears from the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party that the defendant-petitioner has filed the application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a malafide intention only to delay the proceedings of the plaintiff and to harass the plaintiff. There is substance in the submission of the learned Advocate as the defendant petitioner has totally failed to show any sufficient ground for transferring the case. 

 29. Having considered the facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record, the learned Assistant Judge committed no error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order dated 11-5-2003 which caused no failure of justice. 

 30. In view of the facts and circumstance of the case and the law bearing on the matter, we find no merit in the Rule which must fail.
